topic.name: Calculating the Equation of a Tangent Line Using Differentiation

question.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = 2x^2 - 5x$ at the point $(3,3).$
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=2x^2-5x.$ Computing the derivative $f'(x)$ gives

\begin{align*} f'(x) = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(2x^2 - 5x\right)= 4x-5. \end{align*}

We then compute $f'(3)$, which gives \begin{align*} f'(3) = 4(3)-5 = 7. \end{align*}

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=7$ and the coordinates of our point $(3, 3),$ and get \begin{align*} y - y_1 &= m(x-x_1) \\ y - (3) &= 7(x-3) \\ y & =7x - 21 +3\\ y & =7x - 18. \end{align*}

example.title: Calculating the Equation of a Tangent Line to a Curve at a Point

question.text: Find where the tangent to the curve $y = x^4-5$ at the point $(-1,-4)$ intersects the $x$-axis.
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=x^4-5.$ Let's first calculate the derivative:

\begin{align*} f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(x^4-5\right) = 4x^3 \end{align*}

So, the slope of the tangent at our point is \[ m=f'(-1) = 4(-1)^3 = -4. \]

Therefore, the equation of the tangent is

\begin{align} y - y_1 &= m(x-x_1) \\ y - (-4) &= -4(x+1) \\ y & = -4x-4-4\\ y &= -4x-8. \end{align}

To find where the tangent line intercepts the $x$-axis, we set $y=0$ and solve:

\begin{align*} 0 & = -4x-8\\ x & = -2 \end{align*}

Therefore, the point of intersection is $\left(-2, 0\right).$

example.title: Determining where a Tangent Line Intersects an Axis

question.text: Find the equation of the tangent to the curve $y = \dfrac{3x + 2}{x^{2}}$ at the point $(-1,-1).$
question.explanation:
Let $f(x)=\dfrac{3x + 2}{x^{2}}.$ Computing the derivative $f'(x)$ gives

\begin{align*} f'(x) & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left(\dfrac{3x + 2}{x^{2}}\right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \dfrac{3}{x} + \dfrac{2}{x^{2}} \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \dfrac{3}{x} \right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( \dfrac{2}{x^{2}} \right) \\[5pt] & = \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( 3x^{-1} \right) + \dfrac {\textrm{d}}{\textrm{d}x} \left( 2x^{-2} \right) \\[5pt] &= -3x^{-2} - 4x^{-3} \\[5pt] &= -\dfrac{3}{x^{2}} - \dfrac{4}{x^{3}}. \end{align*}

We then compute $f'(-1)$, which gives \begin{align*} f'(-1) &= -\dfrac{3}{(-1)^{2}} - \dfrac{4}{(-1)^{3}} \\[5pt] &= -3 + 4 \\[5pt] &= 1. \end{align*}

Finally, we use the point-slope form with $m=1$ and the coordinates of our point $(-1,-1),$ and get \begin{align*} y - y_{1} &= m(x-x_{1}) \\[5pt] y - (-1) &= 1\cdot (x-(-1)) \\[5pt] y + 1 &= x + 1 \\[5pt] y &= \bbox[4pt, border: 1px solid lightgray]{x}. \end{align*}
